items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: I made Pierron get the old man, see, because he was the style drummer we needed in that band, see.

ctx.x: Yeah, he taught himself. He used good piano players, yeah. Couldn't read though, you know. Couldn't read, Steve Lewis. He had a wonderful ear, you know, gifted, you know. If we played a stock, well we had all good men, you know. And we played down once, he had it, you know. He knew all the chords and everything, you see.
How did you meet Lewis Cattrall?
Well Lewis was a baby when I was playing with his daddy.

items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: We had a four-piece combination there, and I played the Banger Madeline, you know. And we had a violin, piano, drums, and mandolin, Piran, you know. Mm-hmm. And Cottrell was on drums, old man Cottrell, you know. Mm-hmm. And a fellow, he died in Chicago called him Frank Ahenia, a piano player.

ctx.x: Had you ever played anything else, guitar, bass?

Well, I played, we played the St. Charles. We had a four-piece combination there, and I played the Banger Madeline, you know. And we had a violin, piano, drums, and mandolin, Piran, you know. Mm-hmm. And Cottrell was on drums, old man Cottrell, you know. Mm-hmm. And a fellow, he died in Chicago called him Frank Ahenia, a piano player. You might have saw him around Chicago.
